status: Exploration only; no shipped identity replacement.
bbox_convention: Half-open [x, y, x+w, y+h]; all tile bboxes are exact crop regions.
palette_reason: No warm accent needed. Night is the palette near-black used for noses and eyes; snow and frost express a winter coat.
rendering: Pillow primitives only. Characters drawn at 2048x2048; all outputs LANCZOS downsampled from unchanged masters.
preview: Catalog gutters are night; transparent tile bboxes retain alpha 0. Snow wordmarks are intended for dark backgrounds.

directions.name: puff
directions.why: A friendly head-only avatar: winter cheek volume and open eyes communicate welcome without props.
directions.distinction: Soft circular head; expression lives in two large eyes.
directions.use: Community avatar, docs welcome, primary mascot beside the existing mark.
directions.tradeoff: Most overtly cute; the round ears can read as a polar bear at tiny sizes.

small_size_assessment.64: Clear cheeks, ears, eyes and muzzle.
small_size_assessment.32: Fox cheek shape survives; eye highlights soften.
small_size_assessment.16: Readable face, but fox species is ambiguous: round ears and muzzle can read as a polar bear. Not an unqualified favicon.

directions.name: perch
directions.why: A whole companion that can sit beside documentation or peek above a panel; posture adds personality beyond a logo.
directions.distinction: Alert seated body, tucked paws and a tail wrapped across the feet.
directions.use: Repo avatar at 48px+, docs companion, release illustrations.
directions.tradeoff: Body reduces available face pixels; more mascot than symbol.

small_size_assessment.64: Seated pose, tail and face remain clear.
small_size_assessment.48: Paws merge slightly; seated silhouette remains clear.
small_size_assessment.32: Tail wrap reads; face becomes secondary.
small_size_assessment.16: Pale seated silhouette survives, but eyes and tail separation become muddy. Too ambiguous for a standalone favicon.

directions.name: drift
directions.why: Quiet reliability expressed by a fox asleep inside its own tail: a calm alternative to an alert guardian.
directions.distinction: Asymmetric curled sleeping body; pose carries the expression.
directions.use: Docs empty states, idle terminal companion, larger stickers.
directions.tradeoff: Suggests rest rather than speed; weak species recognition when reduced.

small_size_assessment.64: Sleeping face and enveloping tail read clearly.
small_size_assessment.48: Curled pose reads; eyelids become delicate.
small_size_assessment.32: Sleep expression fades; tail remains a crescent.
small_size_assessment.16: Unreadable as a fox: a pale curled smudge with a dark notch. Reject as favicon; keep as an illustration option.

directions.name: beacon
directions.why: A bridge from the current geometric identity to a friendly mascot: fewer large shapes, broad eye spacing, and no decorative details.
directions.distinction: Compact graphic face with rounded ear caps, two-tone cheeks and bold eyes.
directions.use: Best favicon candidate, repo avatar, compact software lockup.
directions.tradeoff: Less expressive than Puff or Perch; still somewhat emblem-like.

small_size_assessment.48: Broad cheeks and dark eyes remain clear.
small_size_assessment.32: Strong face and muzzle; minimal detail loss.
small_size_assessment.16: Best of the four: eyes, nose and broad ears remain separated. Still reads as a face more readily than an unmistakable fox; stronger candidate than proof of species recognition.

reasons: Beacon best preserves face structure at 16px and bridges software mark and mascot.
Puff is the friendliest avatar; use at 32px+ where the face has room.
Perch offers richer companion poses but needs more pixels.
Drift is distinctive at illustration size; unsuitable for a favicon.
recommendation.deployment: Consider Beacon as a replacement candidate or Puff as a companion to the current mark; no replacement authorized.

tiles.name: compare-row
tiles.optical_normalization: Equal alpha-weighted visible area: approximately 54000 px per character, centered in five equal cells.
